title: Go has more positions than the universe has atoms
summary: A 19 by 19 Go board has about 2.08 times 10 to the 170 legal positions. The observable universe holds roughly 10 to the 80 atoms.

beats.say: A Go board has more positions than the universe has atoms.
Each point is empty, black or white.
Legal positions were counted in twenty sixteen.
About two times ten to the power one hundred seventy.
Atoms in the universe: about ten to the eighty.
One position per atom would fall short.

claims.note: Wikipedia, Go and mathematics: the standard board is 19 by 19
Tromp: the number of legal 19x19 positions was determined to be 2081681993819799846..., about 2.08 x 10^170
Tromp: the number of atoms in the universe is only 10^80; Wikipedia gives about 10^80 for the observable universe
Wikipedia, Go and mathematics: 3^361, about 1.74 x 10^172 possible colorings of the board

facts.claim: John Tromp's count of legal positions on a 19x19 Go board is about 2.08 x 10^170, and the number of atoms in the universe is given as 10^80
facts.note: Tromp (2016): L19 determined to be 2081681993819799846...; 'the number of atoms in the universe is only 10^80'

facts.claim: About 2.08 x 10^170 of the roughly 1.74 x 10^172 possible colorings of a 19x19 board are legal positions, about 1.2 percent, and the atom count in the observable universe is about 10^80
facts.note: Wikipedia, Go and mathematics: legal positions are 1.20% of the 3^361 colorings; observable universe about 10^80 atoms
